place.title: Place {ref} (ir obstacle sensor)
place.text: Push {ref}'s 3 pins into column f, one pin per row: OUT into {hole.out}, GND into {hole.gnd}, VCC into {hole.vcc}. The two round parts (the IR light and its sensor) point up, away from the breadboard.
place.tip: Read the labels printed next to the pins. If yours are in another order, follow the labels, not the picture.

why: {ref} shines invisible infrared light forward and watches for it bouncing back: when something is close enough, it pulls its OUT pin LOW and its second LED lights.

wire.ground: This connects {ref}'s GND pin to ground.
wire.power: This powers {ref} from 3.3 V, so its output signal is never more than the Pico's 3.3 V.
wire.in: {pin} reads {ref}'s OUT: 0 while something is in front of the sensor, 1 while the way is clear. The module drives this line itself.
